facts: This is an appeal by special leave from a judgment of the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

The appellants were tried under Section 302, 325 and 323 read with S.34 of the Indian Penal Code by the Additional Sessions Judge, Rohtak for having injured Phusa on January 29, 1966, at about 8 or 8-30 A.M. and when his brother Har Narain intervened he was attacked and he ultimately died on January 31,1966.
Phusa and Ram Sarup had simple injuries.
Out of the appellants Bhima had a contusion mark on the upper corner of the forehead, of a simple nature.
Kishna appellant who is stated to be 18 years old at the time of the incident and who is son of Bhima had a simple injury.
Sohan appellant who is the brother of Bhima had three injuries which were simple.
Sampat's sister's son of Bhima and Sohan who was also quite young, his age being between 17 to 20 years, sustained injuries which were simple.

According to the case of the prosecution one Smt. Misro had filed a complaint against the appellants u/s.504 of the Penal Code in which Phusa P.W.1 helped her and had accompanied her to court on several occasions.
The appellants were discharged in that case on January 28, 1966.
It was alleged that the appellants nursed a grudge against Phusa.

On January 29, 1966 as he was going from his nauhra to his house and was passing in front of the house of Chhajju P.W. the four appellants came there from the side of Chander's house armed with lathis.
Phusa raised an alarm whereupon Bhima gave lathi blow on his left leg.
Kishan followed him by inflicting an injury on his hand.
Another blow was given to Phusa on his back.
Chhaju, Huka, Chand Gorkhi P.Ws. arrived on the scene.
Ram Sarup inquired from the appellants why Phusa was being beaten.
Thereupon he was attacked by the appellants and was given 5-6 stick blows.
Similarly when Har Narain tried to intervene he was attacked.
Bhima and Kishna gave one blow each on his head and after he fell down Kishan gave another blow on his head.
Har Narain, as already stated, died on January 31, 1966 after he had been removed to the Civil Hospital at Newari.
The appellants set up the plea that the injuries which had been caused to the members of the complainant's party were inflicted in exercise of the right of self-defence.
Smt. Kalawati had only been accidentally hit.
issues: Whether S.325 can be applied in this case read with S.34 of the Indian Penal Code

Whether the High Court was right in applying S.34 for convicting the appellants u/s.325 for the injury caused to Kalawati when it had been established that it was appellant No.2, Sohan who had caused that injury
Whether the High Court was right in applying S.34 for convicting all the appellants u/s.325 for causing a grievous injury to Ram Sarup who came to the scene during the course of the scuffle
petitioner_arguments: The learned Additional Sessions Judge found that Ram Sarup and Kalawati P.W. had one serious injury on their persons which had been caused by a blunt weapon and therefore an offence u/s.325 of the Code had been committed in respect of them.
Phusa had three simple injuries on him person caused by a blunt weapon.
As all the four accused persons had common intention, they were liable to be punished u/s.325 and 323 read with S.34 of the Indian Penal Code.
respondent_arguments: The learned Additional Sessions Judge although was of the view that there was no such material, yet on extraneous circumstances he applied S.34 to Ram Pat and Sohan.

I am, therefore, of the opinion that their conviction and sentence under Section 304, read with Section 34, of the Code, has to be set aside-see in this connection, Pandurang v. State of Hyderabad, 1954 Indlaw SC 173.
court_reasoning: The meeting of the minds of the accused can take place even at the spur of the moment, but there should be some substance on the basis of which one could come to that conclusion.
There is no doubt that these two appellants had the common intention to cause at least grievous injuries or had the knowledge that it was likely that grievous injury would be caused.
As regards the first point it has been established by the prosecution that Bhima and Krishna both gave blows with lathis on the head of Har Narayan.

Although originally the concerted attack was on Phusa alone who sustained simple injuries, the common intention on the part of Bhima and Krishna to inflict grievous injuries on Har Narayan can be inferred from their actual acts, namely, of aiming the blows on the head of Har Narayan.
holding: The result is that Ram Pat and Sohan are acquitted of the charge u/s.304 Part I/34, and the conviction of Bhima and Kishna from the above charge is altered to the one under Section 325/34 with the sentence indicated above.
The conviction and sentences of the appellants in respect of all the other charges is hereby set aside.
